# The Box That Changed the World

In 1956, a trucking businessman named Malcom McLean had a simple idea. Why load a ship one sack at a time, when you could lift the whole trailer on board?

On April 26th, the Ideal X left Newark carrying fifty-eight metal boxes. Five days later, it arrived in Houston.

Loading loose cargo cost about $5.86 per ton. With containers, it dropped to roughly sixteen cents.

Ports that refused to change slowly emptied. Ports that adapted became giants.

Today, the biggest ships carry more than twenty-four thousand containers. And almost everything you own spent part of its life inside one of those boxes.
